title: Reference
text: Every exported name, grouped by what it is for. Implementation internals — the CAM16 intermediates and the gamut solver's helpers — are documented in the source but deliberately kept out of the manual.

title: MaterialDesignColors
text: MaterialDesignColors A pure-Julia implementation of the HCT color space and the Material Design 3 color system: CAM16 appearance modelling, tonal palettes, scheme generation, and WCAG contrast helpers. Ported from Google's material-color-utilities (Apache-2.0). See NOTICE.

title: MaterialDesignColors.HCT
text: HCT A color in the HCT (Hue, Chroma, Tone) perceptual color space. Fields hue::Float64: 0–360 (circular). The perceived color on the color wheel.chroma::Float64: 0–~113 (gamut-dependent max). Saturation intensity.tone::Float64: 0 (black)–100 (white). Perceptual lightness (CIE L*).

title: MaterialDesignColors.HCT
text: Tuple{Real, Real, Real} HCT(hue, chroma, tone) Construct an HCT color. Values are stored as-is; use to_hex to convert to sRGB (which may gamut-map the chroma if needed).

title: MaterialDesignColors.hct
text:
Tuple{AbstractString} hct(hex::AbstractString) → HCT Parse a hex color string (e.g. "#6750A4") to the HCT color space. Examples c = hct("#6750A4")
# HCT(281.8, 46.3, 40.0)  (approximately)

title: MaterialDesignColors.hct
text: Tuple{ColorTypes.Colorant} hct(c::Colorant) -> HCT Convert any color from the ColorTypes ecosystem into HCT.

title: MaterialDesignColors.to_hex
text: Tuple{ColorTypes.Colorant} to_hex(c::Colorant) -> String Format any color from the ColorTypes ecosystem as an uppercase #RRGGBB.

title: MaterialDesignColors.to_hex
text: Tuple{HCT} to_hex(c::HCT) → String Convert an HCT color to the closest sRGB hex string ("#RRGGBB"). If the requested chroma is not achievable in sRGB, the maximum achievable chroma at the given hue and tone is used instead. Examples to_hex(HCT(281.8, 46.3, 40.0))  # "#6750A4" (approximately)

title: MaterialDesignColors.TonalPalette
text: Tuple{Real, Real} TonalPalette(hue, chroma) Create a tonal palette from explicit hue and chroma values.

title: MaterialDesignColors.precompute!
text: Tuple{TonalPalette} precompute!(p::TonalPalette) Eagerly compute and cache all standard MD3 tone stops.

title: MaterialDesignColors.tonal_palette
text:

p[90]  # light …

title: MaterialDesignColors.tone_at
text: Tuple{TonalPalette, Int64} tone_at(p::TonalPalette, tone::Int) → HCT Alias for p[tone].

title: MaterialDesignColors.color_scheme
text: Tuple{AbstractString} color_scheme(seed; dark=false, secondary=nothing, tertiary=nothing) Generate the 34 MD3 color roles from seed, as RGB{Float64} values. Use hex_scheme when you need CSS hex strings instead.

title: MaterialDesignColors.color_scheme_pair
text: Tuple{AbstractString} color_scheme_pair(seed; secondary=nothing, tertiary=nothing) The light and dark schemes for one seed, as RGB{Float64} values.

title: MaterialDesignColors.hex_scheme
text:
Tuple{AbstractString} color_scheme(seed; dark=false, secondary=nothing, tertiary=nothing,
             contrast=:standard) → Dict{Symbol,String} Generate a complete MD3 color scheme (29+ roles) from a seed color. Arguments seed::AbstractString: Primary seed hex color (e.g. …

title: MaterialDesignColors.hex_scheme_pair
text:
Tuple{AbstractString} color_scheme_pair(seed; secondary=nothing, tertiary=nothing,
                  contrast=:standard) → (light, dark) Generate both light and dark color schemes in one call. Returns a tuple of (light_scheme, dark_scheme).

title: MaterialDesignColors.contrast_ratio
text: Tuple{AbstractString, AbstractString} contrast_ratio(hex1::AbstractString, hex2::AbstractString) → Float64 Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two hex colors. Returns a value in [1, 21]. A ratio ≥ 4.5 meets WCAG AA for normal text; ≥ 3.0 meets AA for large text; ≥ 7.0 meets AAA. …

title: MaterialDesignColors.contrast_ratio
text: Tuple{Float64, Float64} contrast_ratio(tone1::Float64, tone2::Float64) → Float64 Compute contrast ratio from two CIE L* tone values (0–100). Useful for checking contrast between HCT tones without converting to hex.

title: MaterialDesignColors.darker_tone
text: Tuple{Float64, Float64} darker_tone(tone::Float64, ratio::Float64) → Float64 Find the darkest tone (in CIE L*) that achieves at least the given contrast ratio against the input tone. Returns NaN if impossible.

title: MaterialDesignColors.lighter_tone
text: Tuple{Float64, Float64} lighter_tone(tone::Float64, ratio::Float64) → Float64 Find the lightest tone (in CIE L*) that achieves at least the given contrast ratio against the input tone. Returns NaN if impossible.

title: MaterialDesignColors.meets_aa
text:
Tuple{AbstractString, AbstractString} meets_aa(hex_fg::AbstractString, hex_bg::AbstractString;
         large_text::Bool=false) → Bool Check if a foreground/background color pair meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements. Normal text requires ≥ 4.5:1; large text requires ≥ 3.0:1.

title: MaterialDesignColors.meets_aaa
text:
Tuple{AbstractString, AbstractString} meets_aaa(hex_fg::AbstractString, hex_bg::AbstractString;
          large_text::Bool=false) → Bool Check if a foreground/background color pair meets WCAG 2.1 AAA contrast requirements. Normal text requires ≥ 7.0:1; large text requires ≥ 4.5:1.

title: Color Engine
text: MaterialDesignColors is a pure-Julia port of Google's material-color-utilities: the CAM16 appearance model, the HCT color space, tonal palettes, Material Design 3 scheme generation, and WCAG contrast helpers.

title: HCT
text: HCT combines the hue and chroma of the CAM16 color appearance model with the lightness (L*) of CIELAB. Its value is that tone maps directly to contrast: two colors 40 tones apart have a predictable contrast ratio regardless of hue. That is what lets a whole palette be generated from one color …

title: Working with the Colorant ecosystem
text:
HCT is a ColorTypes.Color{Float64,3}, so it dispatches anywhere a Colorant is accepted and converts to and from the RGB family: using MaterialDesignColors, Colors

convert(RGB, hct("#6750A4"))     # RGB{Float64}(0.404, 0.314, 0.643)
hct(colorant"rebeccapurple")     # HCT from any Colorant Every …

title: Tonal palettes
text:
A TonalPalette is one hue and chroma sampled across the tone range: p = tonal_palette("#6750A4")
tone_at(p, 40)           # HCT at tone 40 — primary in a light scheme
to_hex(tone_at(p, 80))   # "#CFBCFF" — primary in a dark scheme
p[90]                    # indexing is an alias for tone_at A …

title: Schemes
text:
color_scheme generates the 34 MD3 roles from a seed, as colors: light = color_scheme("#6750A4")
dark  = color_scheme("#6750A4"; dark = true)

light[:primary]              # RGB{Float64}
light[:on_primary_container] color_scheme_pair returns both at once. When you need CSS strings rather than …

title: Contrast
text:
contrast_ratio("#FFFFFF", "#6750A4")   # 6.44
meets_aa("#FFFFFF", "#6750A4")         # true

title: Why HCT
text: HCT pairs the hue and chroma of CAM16 with the lightness (L*) of CIELAB. The useful consequence is that tone maps directly to contrast: two colors a fixed distance apart in tone have a predictable contrast ratio regardless of hue. title: Installation
text:
MaterialDesignColors is not yet registered in the General registry, so add it by URL: using Pkg
Pkg.add(url = "https://github.com/mthelm85/MaterialDesignColors.jl.git")

title: Works with the Colorant ecosystem
text: HCT is a ColorTypes.Color{Float64,3}, so it converts to and from the RGB family and passes anywhere a Colorant is accepted — including into Makie themes, ColorSchemes.jl, and Plots. Environments that render color swatches show HCT values as swatches rather than numbers.
